description: Remotely triggerable uncaught exception in TLS servers
overview: A deferred-callback use-after-destroy in Node.js TLS server handshake handling allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to terminate the server process. When a TLS server uses any of the `SNICallback`, `OCSPRequest`, `newSession`, or `resumeSession` hooks, or `server.addContext()`, the corresponding OpenSSL callbacks are deferred, and the deferred code does not handle the underlying socket being destroyed between scheduling and execution. By sending a client hello that reaches the vulnerable path (for example, no SNI together with an OCSP request) followed by padding and a socket FIN, an attacker makes OpenSSL deliver the client hello and the end-of-file in the same tick, so the socket is destroyed before the deferred callback runs and the process raises an uncaught exception instead of emitting an `'error'` event. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.
